name: Office of the Registrar of Companies
mandate: Registers business names, companies and partnerships, maintains the companies register, and receives annual returns and beneficial ownership filings. Formerly the Registrar-General's Department (RGD).
head_office: Opposite the Ghana News Agency, inside the Registrar-General's Department premises, P.O. Box 2559, Accra

name: Ghana Revenue Authority
mandate: Administers domestic taxes and customs. Issues Taxpayer Identification Numbers to organisations, registers taxpayers for VAT and other tax types, and operates the taxpayers' portal.
head_office: Off Starlet 91 Road, Ministries, Accra. P.O. Box 2202, Accra
offices: TIN Centres in Accra and Tema

name: National Identification Authority
mandate: Registers Ghanaians and legally resident foreign nationals, maintains the National Identity Register, and issues the Ghana Card. The Ghana Card PIN also serves as the Taxpayer Identification Number for individuals.
head_office: No. 8 Nelson Mandela Avenue, South Legon, Accra

name: Passport Office, Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Regional Integration
mandate: Issues Ghanaian passports and travel documents, and operates the online passport application system and application centres.
head_office: Passport Head Office, Accra (reported to operate 24 hours)
opening_hours: Head office operates 24 hours; application centres during office hours
offices: 14 application centres including Accra, Ridge, Tema, Kumasi, Takoradi, Sunyani, Ho, Tamale, Koforidua, Cape Coast and Wa
Premium centres in Accra, Kumasi and Tamale
notes: The live official domain is passport.mfa.gov.gh. Any site claiming to be passport.gov.gh is not an official Passport Office portal.

name: Driver and Vehicle Licensing Authority
mandate: Licenses drivers and vehicles, registers vehicles, certifies roadworthiness, and registers driving schools and instructors. Established by the DVLA Act 569 (1999); operates under the Road Traffic Regulations, 2012 (L.I. 2180).
offices: Over 50 service centres across all 16 regions

name: Social Security and National Insurance Trust
mandate: Administers the basic national social security scheme under the National Pensions Act, 2008 (Act 766). Registers employers and members and collects Tier 1 contributions.

name: Births and Deaths Registry
mandate: Registers births and deaths occurring in Ghana and issues birth and death certificates and certified copies.
head_office: Accra (street address not published on the official site)
offices: District offices nationwide - a birth must be registered in the district where it occurred

name: National Health Insurance Authority
mandate: Administers the National Health Insurance Scheme, registers and renews members, accredits providers and pays claims.
phone: Not published on the official website
head_office: Accra (contact page not published in a retrievable form)

name: Ghana Police Service
mandate: Maintains law and order. The Criminal Data Service Bureau of the CID conducts criminal record checks and issues police clearance certificates.
offices: Nima Divisional Police Headquarters, Accra (police clearance)

name: Ghana Post Company Limited
mandate: Operates the national postal service and owns GhanaPostGPS, the national digital addressing system that assigns a permanent address to every 5m x 5m square in the country.
opening_hours: App and web map available at all times

name: Accra Metropolitan Assembly
mandate: The local authority for the Accra Metropolis. Issues business operating permits and development or building permits, and collects property rates. Used here as the worked example for all 261 Metropolitan, Municipal and District Assemblies.
head_office: H72 Independence Avenue, Kinbu Garden, Accra. P.O. Box GP 385, Accra Central
notes: Ghana has 261 MMDAs. Each sets its own permit fees annually through a fee-fixing resolution, so no national figure exists.

name: Lands Commission
mandate: Manages public lands, maintains the land register, and conducts official searches on land title.

name: Environmental Protection Authority
mandate: Issues environmental permits and regulates activities with environmental impact.

name: Ghana National Fire Service
mandate: Fire safety certification and inspection of premises and building plans.

name: Food and Drugs Authority
mandate: Registers food, drugs, herbal and homeopathic medicines, vaccines and biological products, medical devices, cosmetics, household chemicals, tobacco and food supplements, and licenses the premises that make them, under the Public Health Act, 2012 (Act 851). Approval is about SAFETY of a regulated product.

name: Ghana Investment Promotion Centre
mandate: Registers enterprises with foreign participation and administers minimum capital requirements for foreign investors.

name: Ghana Immigration Service
mandate: Manages entry, residence and work permits for non-Ghanaians, and border control.

name: National Pensions Regulatory Authority
mandate: Regulates occupational pension schemes, including the Tier 2 schemes employers must arrange with licensed corporate trustees.

name: Land Use and Spatial Planning Authority
mandate: Sets national spatial planning standards and development permitting guidelines that District Planning Authorities apply.

name: National Information Technology Agency
mandate: Digital government infrastructure and standards, including the Ghana.GOV service and payment platform.

name: Ghana Ports and Harbours Authority
mandate: Builds, operates, maintains and regulates Ghana's seaports at Tema and Takoradi. GPHA handles the ship, the berth and the cargo on the terminal - it does not clear goods through customs, which is GRA Customs Division's job.
offices: Port of Tema - P.O. Box 488, Tema, +233 (0) 303 219120
Port of Takoradi - P.O. Box 708, Takoradi, +233 (0) 3120 24073
notes: People routinely believe GPHA clears their goods. It does not. Route clearance questions to GRA Customs and name GPHA for what it actually controls: the port, the terminal and the handling charges.

name: Ministry of Trade and Industry
mandate: The ministry responsible for trade policy. It issues the Import Declaration Form (IDF) that a customs declaration requires.
notes: Tier 2 directory entry. Named because the IDF is a documented requirement for import clearance.

name: Ghana Standards Authority
mandate: Sets national standards and certifies that a product conforms to them, awarding the Standard Mark. Also inspects imports. Certification is about CONFORMITY to a standard - a different question from whether a regulated product is safe to sell, which is the FDA's.
notes: Tier 2 directory entry, named as a possible permit issuer in the import clearance path.
